narrative:
The model estimates a 57% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Most influential was the number of training programs you attended over the past three years. With seven or more programs completed, you stand out from the typical employee predicted to stay, most of whom attended far fewer. Surprisingly, this high participation pushed the model toward predicting you would leave. The system appears to interpret extensive recent training as a sign that you are preparing for opportunities elsewhere.

Your total years of professional experience came next in importance. At 6–10 years, you have more experience than half the employees the model expects to stay. This longer track record also nudged the prediction toward leaving, suggesting the model sees seasoned professionals as more likely to move on.

Finally, your time with this current organization (1–5 years) added further weight toward departure. While many who stay have similar tenure, the combination with your broader experience signaled higher mobility risk to the model.

The organization should review whether your extensive training is truly preparing you for growth here or elsewhere, and consider clearer promotion pathways for experienced staff. You may want to discuss your long-term goals openly with your manager to align expectations.
